title: SLO / Error Budget Escalation Intake Template (Customer Success)
content:
Purpose
Use this template whenever a customer escalation references SLOs, SLAs, “error budget”, availability/5xx, latency spikes, or streaming disconnects. The goal is to collect the minimum data SRE/Platform needs to (a) validate impact against canonical SLIs, (b) quickly identify top contributing routes/models/regions, and (c) determine whether the event triggers an incident per the error budget policy.

When to use
- Dedicated customer reports elevated 5xx, sustained latency regression, or throughput collapse
- Hosted customer reports repeated disconnects on streaming or major latency spikes during burst traffic
- Customer asks “are we breaching SLO/SLA?” or requests an error budget status snapshot

Where to file
- Create/attach to the customer-facing Support ticket (Jira) AND create an internal incident/escalation thread as needed.
- Paste the completed intake into the ticket description. If sensitive data (prompt content, PHI) is involved, do NOT paste request bodies; include IDs only.


SECTION 1 — Customer + Contract Context
1) Company / Account name:
- 

2) Customer contact(s) and channel:
- (name, email, Slack Connect channel, phone bridge if any)

3) Deployment tier (select one):
- [ ] Hosted (shared)
- [ ] Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- [ ] Unsure (need help determining)

4) Region(s) impacted (select all that apply):
- [ ] us-east
- [ ] us-west
- [ ] eu-west
- [ ] eu-central
- [ ] ap-southeast
- [ ] Other: 

5) Business impact (customer words if possible):
- What is broken? (login blocked, chat feature down, batch pipeline failing, etc.)
- Estimated $ impact or user impact (if provided):
- Is this production or staging?:

6) Severity (CS initial classification):
- [ ] Sev-1 (customer production down / major outage)
- [ ] Sev-2 (severe degradation, workaround exists)
- [ ] Sev-3 (minor degradation / intermittent)

7) Time sensitivity:
- Do they need an update cadence? (e.g., every 30 minutes)
- Next customer meeting / executive escalation deadline:


SECTION 2 — What exactly is failing (SLI framing)
Select the primary symptom(s):
- [ ] Elevated 5xx (non-streaming)
- [ ] Elevated 5xx during streaming initiation
- [ ] Streaming disconnects mid-stream
- [ ] Latency regression (p95/p99)
- [ ] Increased timeouts
- [ ] Throughput/TPM lower than expected
- [ ] Intermittent errors (bursty)
- [ ] Other:

Endpoint class (select one):
- [ ] Chat/Completions (non-streaming)
- [ ] Chat/Completions (streaming)
- [ ] Embeddings
- [ ] Rerank
- [ ] Unsure

Customer expectation framing:
- Are they referencing an SLA clause, or asking “are you meeting SLO”?:
- Any specific numbers quoted by customer? (e.g., “p95 must be < 1.5s”):


SECTION 3 — Time window + reproducibility (most important)
1) Incident time window (include timezone; use ISO-8601 if possible):
- Start time:
- End time (or “ongoing”):
- Timezone:

2) Is the issue ongoing right now?
- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- If yes: are they able to pause/slow traffic?

3) Reproducibility:
- [ ] Consistent (every request)
- [ ] Intermittent
- [ ] Only during bursts
- [ ] Only specific routes/models

4) Request volume context:
- Approx RPS or requests/min during the window:
- Approx tokens/sec or TPM (if known):
- Any known traffic changes (feature launch, batch job, marketing event):


SECTION 4 — Technical identifiers to find the traffic
Provide as many as possible. These enable trace/log correlation and accurate SLI accounting.

1) Request IDs (REQUIRED: at least 3; ideally 10–20 spanning the window)
- Request ID(s):
  - 
  - 
  - 

2) Trace / Span IDs (if customer has them):
- 

3) Customer identifiers
- Organization / project ID in our system:
- Dedicated cluster name (if Dedicated):
- API key name/label (do NOT paste raw secrets):

4) Models and versions
- Model name(s):
- Model version or alias (if pinned):
- Any recent model change? (e.g., moved from model A to model B):

5) Parameters that may matter
- Streaming: on/off:
- Max output tokens:
- Typical input length (approx tokens):
- Temperature/top_p (only if relevant):

6) Example request (SAFE VERSION)
- Provide a redacted curl/SDK snippet OR a minimal reproduction description.
- Do NOT paste prompt contents for regulated customers; provide schema/size only.


SECTION 5 — Symptoms detail (pick relevant subsection)
A) Elevated 5xx
- Error code(s) seen (e.g., 500/502/503):
- Error message(s) (verbatim):
- Are errors concentrated to one region or global?:
- Are retries succeeding?:

B) Latency regression
- Customer-reported metrics (p50/p95/p99) and measurement method:
- Where are they measuring from? (client-side, server-reported, APM)
- Is the latency pre-first-token (TTFT) or total time?:

C) Streaming disconnects
- How does the disconnect appear? (socket closed, incomplete JSON, SSE terminated)
- Does disconnect happen at start or mid-stream?:
- Approx % of streams impacted:
- Client library and version (if known):
- Did customer implement reconnect/retry?:

D) Timeouts
- Timeout threshold on client:
- Any proxy/CDN in front (Cloudflare, API gateway on their side):


SECTION 6 — Exclusions / classification hints (to avoid misrouting)
Answer these quick checks (best effort). These help distinguish “counts against SLO” vs excluded traffic.
- Any evidence requests are malformed (4xx validation errors)?:
- Any evidence they are rate-limited (429 / quota exceeded)?:
- Any evidence the client is aborting the request (navigation away / client timeout)?:
- Any evidence they are intentionally canceling streams?:

Note: SLO success rate generally focuses on server-side failures (non-5xx is success for availability), while latency SLOs are computed on successful requests per canonical SLI definitions. Streaming reliability uses server disconnect/error events, excluding confirmed client aborts where possible.


SECTION 7 — Dashboards and links (REQUIRED for escalations)
Paste direct links and/or screenshots. If you don’t have access, request access via internal helpdesk and note it here.

1) Redwood Console / Tiered SLO dashboard link
- Link:
- Filters applied (tier, region, model, endpoint):

2) Traces/logs link (if available)
- Link:

3) Any relevant status page or incident link
- Link:

4) Slack threads / internal comms
- Link to Slack thread in #support / #eng-sre / #incidents:


SECTION 8 — Actions already taken (so we don’t duplicate)
- Did CS/Solutions Engineering recommend retries/backoff?:
- Did we advise region failover or model fallback?:
- Any mitigation already applied by SRE/Platform (rollback, capacity add, routing change)?:
- Customer workaround in place?:


SECTION 9 — Escalation routing (CS instructions)
Fill this out, then route based on tier and symptom.

1) Primary owner to page/engage
- Dedicated + 5xx/latency or sustained budget burn: engage SRE on-call + Dedicated PM escalation if customer-facing comms required
- Hosted widespread or multi-region: engage SRE on-call; if streaming disconnects, include Routing/Control Plane on-call

2) Provide the one-paragraph summary for engineering (copy/paste)
“Between <start> and <end> (<timezone>), <customer> (<tier>) experienced <symptom> in <region(s)> for <endpoint/model>. Impact: <business impact>. Evidence: <# of request IDs> request IDs and dashboard link <url>. Customer asks for <SLO/SLA status / mitigation / ETA>.”

3) Required attachments before paging (minimum bar)
- [ ] Time window with timezone
- [ ] ≥3 request IDs
- [ ] Region(s)
- [ ] Endpoint class (chat/embeddings/streaming)
- [ ] Model name(s)
- [ ] Dashboard link (or note “no access yet” + helpdesk ticket)


SECTION 10 — Customer comms notes (for CS)
- What we can say immediately:
  - We’re investigating using request IDs + internal SLO dashboards; we will confirm scope (region/model) and share mitigation options.
- What NOT to commit to:
  - Do not promise SLA credits, SLO breach, or specific root cause until SRE confirms.
- Preferred update cadence (if Sev-1/2):
  - Every 30–60 minutes or aligned to incident updates.


Appendix — Quick examples (for reference)
Example A (Dedicated 5xx)
- Window: 2026-02-11T18:05Z–19:20Z
- Region: eu-west
- Endpoint: streaming chat
- Models: rw-llama-70b-v3
- Request IDs: 12 attached
- Symptom: ~8–12% 502s + intermittent stream disconnects
- Link: Console SLO dashboard filtered to Dedicated/eu-west/streaming

Example B (Hosted latency)
- Window: ongoing, started 2026-02-03 09:10 PST
- Regions: us-east only
- Endpoint: non-streaming chat/completions
- Symptom: p95 jumped from ~900ms to ~2.8s; 5xx normal
- Link: Hosted latency dashboard + trace sample IDs

Change log
- 2026-02-14: Added explicit streaming disconnect details + exclusion questions (client abort vs server disconnect). Added minimum paging bar + summary paragraph.
